payload.detail: tmux_adapter.py:285 sends the message and Enter in ONE send-keys call: _tmux("send-keys","-t",target,args.message,"Enter"). Against the codex TUI the Enter is absorbed (bracketed-paste race) - the text lands in the input buffer and just sits there. The adapter prints "nudged <agent> at <target>" and exits 0 regardless, so a nudge that did nothing is indistinguishable from one that worked. Observed 2026-07-28 spawning codex-bus-tests: the brief sat unsubmitted at the prompt until a separate `tmux send-keys -t <target> Enter` was issued manually.
payload.impact: This is the same fail-open shape as C3. OP-SENDKEYS-CODEX was granted specifically so the daemon could nudge a main; every nudge the stall ladder sends may be silently landing in a buffer instead of being acted on, while the ledger records a successful nudge. Any stall-ladder evidence gathered so far should be treated as unverified.
payload.owner: unassigned - not fixed by coordinator-agent this session
payload.suggested_fix: Send the message, then Enter as a SEPARATE send-keys after a short delay, and verify submission by re-capturing the pane and confirming the prompt buffer no longer holds the text - report failure rather than exit 0 blind.
payload.title: tmux_adapter nudge reports success but the message is never submitted

payload.detail: heartbeats/ contains 22 files whose names are task ids, not roster ids: checkpoint_wrapup_tb6_m2_v2, e5_pre_reboot_prep, e8_generation_tail_resume, e8_launch_sequence_review, e8_new_head_rearm_review, e8_partial_r2_recovery, e8_r2_execute_test_and_fix, e8_r2_failure_recovery_semantics, e8_r2_salvage_extension, e8_recovery_finalizer_validator, e8_t1_core_fix_review, e8_terminal_validation_prep, e8_v5_runtime_root_fix, episodic_reseed_terminal, ff_pair_provenance, fg4b_evidence_importer, g3_context_defect_fix, g3_postrag_queue_prep, g3_runner_independent_review, refresh_gpu_queue_integration, validate_reseed_integration, wrap_ff_boundary.
payload.impact: BUS_PROTOCOL rule 1 defines heartbeats/<w> as owned by WRITER <w>. A per-task heartbeat has no writer, so single-writer ownership is undefined for these files and the ownership lint cannot evaluate them. They also inflate the agent roster that `rebuild` and the daemon derive - session_bus.py rebuild already lists refresh_gpu_queue_integration and validate_reseed_integration as though they were agents, which means stall-ladder and idle accounting are computed over phantom agents that will never respond to a nudge. That directly contaminates M4 zero-idle acceptance evidence.
payload.note: Not fixed by coordinator-agent: these are other sessions files and deleting them is destructive. Likely a misreading of the heartbeat contract as per-task rather than per-writer - task identity belongs in the task_id FIELD, which the schema already carries.
payload.title: 22 heartbeat files are keyed by TASK, not by writer

payload.detail: claude-main is rostered endpoint monitor:file, drain: push. A task-assign relayed to its inbox at 16:21Z (e5-stage-b-plan-provenance-repair) was still unread minutes later: rebuild shows claude-main state=idle task=None unread=1, cursor stuck at 13006. Nothing pushes to a monitor:file endpoint and the agent is idle so it never hits a boundary that would drain. tmux_adapter also refuses it - not a tmux endpoint - so it cannot be nudged either. The message is delivered-but-undeliverable.
payload.impact: An idle monitor:file agent is unreachable by BOTH channels: no push, no nudge. Work assigned to it silently rots. This is distinct from C1/C2 (which were about the relay existing at all) - here the relay works and the endpoint is the dead end. Any coordinator assignment to claude-main today should be treated as NOT dispatched until it acks. It also means the stall ladder cannot recover such an agent, which contaminates M4 acceptance the same way C7 did.
payload.note: Operator identified claude-main as the pane agent:claude_A. Coordinator deliberately did NOT re-point the roster endpoint to tmux:agent:claude_A: the identity is inferred, not proven, and a wrong endpoint means send-keys into the wrong pane - the exact failure tmux_adapter exists to prevent. Coordinator also declined to send-keys into that pane directly because it held operator-typed text in its input buffer plus a live background agent; typing would have corrupted the operators own in-flight input.
payload.suggested_fix: Either give monitor:file a real push mechanism, or make it a rostered tmux endpoint so the nudge ladder can reach it. Until then, validate should WARN on any roster row whose endpoint has no working delivery path, rather than letting assignments accumulate unread.
payload.title: endpoint monitor:file provides no actual delivery path - assignments rot unread

payload.procedure: Need a reload while someone holds inference? Do NOT run it. Send a request to coordinator-agent naming what needs reloading and why; the coordinator routes it to the owning session, which schedules it into its own workflow and reports when done. Waiting is correct behaviour, not a blocker - work the next queued item meanwhile (never block, BUS_PROTOCOL rule 2).
payload.rule: If a session OWNS the inference, any orchestrator API or stack reload must be executed BY THAT SESSION, at a point it chooses when it can be squeezed in. A reload is never forced upon its workflow from outside. This is the drain-at-boundary axiom applied to the API: quiesce and let the holder release at ITS boundary, never preempt.
payload.standing: This rule outlives the current E8 run. It is not a temporary freeze - it is how reloads work whenever any session holds inference.
